start.responsibility: Entry-point task node that captures the user's request to design the detailed logic of an e-commerce order processing module (state machine + Saga + layered fallback).
start.implementation: Treated as a pure orchestration origin: it holds the high-level objective and forwards flow to downstream deliverable nodes without carrying domain logic itself.
start.design_intent: Establishes a single, traceable starting point for the design effort so downstream artifact nodes (Mermaid state machine, order-detail sub-graph, high-level abstract steps) can be reasoned about as branches of one explicit ask.
start.constraints: Pure entry node with no domain payload; must not embed implementation specifics; only outgoing edge is to the deliverable — semantic content lives downstream.

deliverable.responsibility: Deliver the final artifact of the order-processing design task: Mermaid source code that pairs a high-level view of the overall order pipeline with an expanded sub-diagram of the order-detail stage.
deliverable.implementation: Typically realized as one or more Mermaid code blocks (stateDiagram / flowchart / sequence) where the main diagram keeps each pipeline step as a single abstract node and the order-detail diagram unpacks that node into a state-machine of order statuses, a Saga sequence of compensating steps, and a layered fallback/retry hierarchy.
deliverable.design_intent: Exists to satisfy a dual-audience deliverable: stakeholders can read the high-level flow to see where order-detail sits in the e-commerce order lifecycle, while implementers can read the detailed sub-diagram to understand the state transitions, distributed-transaction compensation, and graceful-degradation strategy that govern that one critical step.
deliverable.constraints: Must be valid Mermaid that renders; must explicitly combine state-machine + Saga + layered-fallback concepts inside the order-detail sub-diagram; other pipeline steps must remain at high-level abstraction (not over-expanded); the artifact is terminal in the task graph (LeadsTo from start only) so it must be self-contained as the hand-off output.
